latest_release.body:
## What's Changed
* Gap 19: ODT parity row says how tab stops are saved by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6094
* ODT: table and row backgrounds show behind their cells (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5727
* ODT: a document keeps its language when styles are rewritten (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5704
* ODT: frames keep the page they are anchored to (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5705
* ODT: pictures keep the size their file gives (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5721
* ODT: custom styles with an outline level keep their name when edited (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5770
* ODT: text can turn off what its style turns on (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5724
* ODT: a font size reaches every script's text (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5728
* ODT: columns stating only their shares keep their proportions (gap 19) by @alehel in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5722
* CLI: --strict on convert and render refuses missing glyphs and pictures (#6005) by @benandez in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6039
* Paste: composite CSS colours with alpha over the page instead of dropping it by @benandez in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6164
* RTF: style-sheet names take Unicode escapes; a malformed \' escape leaks no bytes by @benandez in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6165
* MacOS: the window moves by its title bar behind a modal dialog (#5124) by @RatkoR in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5125
* sonar: SHA-1 in ODT decryption is the format's, not a choice by @FredApps in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6187
* packaging: use [[ for bash tests (SonarCloud S7688) by @dylanmtaylor in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6224
* Clipboard: size-check a Wayland clipboard picture before anything decodes it by @dylanmtaylor in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/5441
* Ribbon: hover fades, group glow, sliding tab underline and a brief content slide by @fluorine in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/3781
* #4501 follow-up: restore pre-refactor behaviour by @benandez in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/4683
* Line numbers appear beside every column and keep their Word formatting by @vangel76 in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6049
* .doc: first body line no longer starts too low under a header by @vangel76 in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6047
* DOCX: save and load tracked revision marks around equations (#6011) by @batistalucasv in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6033
* fix(wordcraft): satisfy clippy on clipboard.rs after #5441 by @FredApps in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6239
* Preserve header/footer content when adding page numbers (#2201) by @MMexicann in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/2251
* backstage: right-align template titles and thumbnails in RTL (#6151) by @batistalucasv in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6163
* Engine: fall back to fsync on Apple targets when full flush is unsupported (#6155) by @batistalucasv in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6161
* Insert > Date & Time: Word-style dialog with regional formats and field support (#5093) by @batistalucasv in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6022
* Refuse ui.screenshot on secondary document windows and support root window selection by @batistalucasv in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6169
* CI: Print installs its Linux packages through the shared fallback mirrors by @FredApps in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/6308
* Linux: stay on native Wayland when the X11 libraries are missing by @bmh129 in https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/pull/3359
* ci: run Harden-Runner on every job by @dylanmtaylor i

detail.readme:
WordCraft

Writing and document design; an open-source, modern word processor, built in pure Rust.

A fast, open-source word processor with a familiar workflow: the ribbon, styles, tables, track changes, references and mail merge. It reads and writes .docx, runs natively on macOS, Windows, Linux and BSD, and in the browser via WebAssembly.
By the ArtCraft team.


WordCraft on getartcraft.com · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



The Open Studio Handbook, WordCraft's built-in sample: the ribbon, live Styles gallery, rulers and the Navigation pane.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

A tour · Why WordCraft · What works today · Quick start · For agents · Architecture · Roadmap · Downloads · The Crafting Apps · License and credits

## A tour Every screenshot below is WordCraft itself, rendered offscreen by its own UI test harness (`cargo run -p wordcraft-ui-egui --example ui_shot`).

Review. Track changes, comment balloons in the margin, accept and reject, spelling and grammar as you type.

References. Tables of contents, footnotes, citations in APA, MLA, Chicago or IEEE, index and captions.

Design. Themes, style sets, paragraph spacing, watermarks, page colour and borders.

Dark mode with formatting marks, and the Insert tab: tables, pictures, shapes, links, headers, footers, fields and symbols.

Layout. Drop caps, text wrapping around pictures and shapes, automatic hyphenation, line numbers and page borders.

File. Start from a template, open recent documents, edit properties, export to PDF and other formats.
## Why WordCraft - **Familiar.** Ribbon tabs, groups, shortcuts and behaviour: Enter continues a list, Tab demotes it, Ctrl/⌘+B bolds the word under the caret, the Styles gallery previews styles live, F4 repeats, F7 checks spelling, F8 extends the selection. - **Your files.** Opens and saves .docx (OOXML), and also .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .tex (LaTeX), .txt; opens legacy 97-2003 .doc; exports PDF with real, selectable text, links and bookmarks. - **Fast.** Paragraph layout is cached, so typing in a 188-page document re-lays it out in about 1.4 ms; pages render on demand. - **Everywhere.** One Rust codebase for macOS, Windows, Linux, BSD and the web. No Electron, no Tauri: native [egui](https://github.com/emilk/egui) on the GPU. - **Built for agents.** Every action is a command with an id. The same 422 commands drive the ribbon, keyboard shortcuts, the command search, a command-line tool, a JSON control channel and an MCP server. - **Private.** Spelling, grammar and everything else work offline. - **Open.** MIT OR Apache-2.0. Clean-room: built from public specifications and observation, with every asset original or openly licensed. ## What works today | Area | Highlights | |---|---| | **Writing** | Fast typing with IME, smart quotes, AutoCorrect, list autoformat (`* `, `1. `), dashes; word, sentence, paragraph selection; drag-select; clipboard with formatting; undo/redo; find and replace with regex | | **Formatting** | Fonts, sizes, bold/italic/underline styles, strike, sub/superscript, caps, highlight, colours, character spacing, Format Painter, Change Case, Clear Formatting | | **Paragraphs** | Alignment, indents (draggable on the ruler), spacing, line spacing, tabs with leaders, borders, shading, keep with next, widow/orphan control | | **Styles** | Built-in style set, live gallery, Styles pane, create/modify/update styles, style sets, themes | | **Lists** | Bullets, numbering, multilevel, restart, set value, custom formats | | **Tables** | Insert by grid, merge/split, styles with banded rows, borders, shading, header rows repeated across pages, rows that split across pages, sort, formulas, text ↔ table | | **Pages** | Margins, orientation, size, columns, page/column/section breaks, headers and footers (first page, odd/even), page numbers, watermark, page borders, line numbers, vertical alignment, drop caps, automatic hyphenation | | **Objects** | Pictures (resize, crop, recolour, brightness/contrast, transparency, background removal, picture styles, rotate), shapes, text boxes, floating position with text wrapping (square, top and bottom, behind or in front of text) | | **References** | Table of contents, footnotes and endnotes, citations and bibliography (APA, MLA, Chicago, IEEE), captions, table of figures, cross-references, index, table of authorities | | **Review** | Spelling and grammar with suggestions (English and Polish, by each run's language), thesaurus, word count, comments in margin balloons or a pane, track changes, accept/reject, compare documents, restrict editing, accessibility checker, document inspector | | **Mailings** | Mail merge from CSV, merge fields, address block, greeting line, rules, preview, finish to a document; envelopes and labels | | **View** | Print layout, web layout, draft, read mode, focus, zoom, one/multiple pages, page width, Navigation pane, rulers, gridlines, dark mode; interface in English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, Português (Brasil), Español, Українська, Српски / Srpski, Eesti, Türkçe, Русский, Italiano, Deutsch, Polski, Čeština, Magyar, Français, Български, Tiếng Việt, 한국어, Svenska, Hrvatski, Nederlands, Dansk, Română, العربية (mirrored) or Slovenščina (follows the system language by default) | | **Files** | .docx read/write, legacy 97-2003 .doc import, PDF export, .odt, .rtf, .html, .md, .tex, .txt import/export, page images | The honest picture, area by area, is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), the [parity assessment](docs/target-app-parity.md) and the generated [feature checklist](docs/parity-checklist.md). ## Quick start ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft cd wordcraft cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample # the desktop app with the sample document cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- report.docx # open a document ``` The interface translations and the spelling and hyphenation data come from [craft-i18n](https://github.com/storytold/craft-i18n), an optional build input. To build with them, check it out at the commit in `craft-i18n.rev` and point `CRAFT_I18N_DIR` at it (an absolute path); without it WordCraft builds with an English interface, English spelling falls back to an installed Hunspell English or craft-proof's built-in word list, and only Bulgarian, Turkish and Russian hyphenate (by rule): ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-i18n ../craft-i18n git -C ../craft-i18n checkout "$(cat craft-i18n.rev)" CRAFT_I18N_DIR="$PWD/../craft-i18n" cargo run --release -p wordcraft -- --sample ``` Command line: ```sh wordcraft-cli convert report.docx report.pdf # docx, pdf, odt, rtf, html, md, tex, txt, png wordcraft-cli convert report.docx report.pdf --strict # exit 3, no file, if a character or picture would be left out wordcraft-cli text report.docx # plain text wordcraft-cli inspect report.docx # structure as JSON wordcraft-cli run --template sample \ --cmd 'select.text={"text":"Membership"}' --cmd format.bold --save out.docx wordcraft-cli run --script job.json # the same from a file: commands, then save to docx and pdf ``` `convert --strict` (a `.pdf` or `.png` output only) and `render --strict` (a PNG of one page) refuse a silently incomplete render: they exit 3 and write nothing if the output would draw a character no font has (an empty box) or leave out a picture. Exit codes are 0 (written), 1 (unreadable input, usage error, or `--strict` with another output type, checked before the input is read) and 3 (strict refusal). On exit 3, stderr has one `wordcraft-cli: strict: …` line per kind, then one JSON line: ```sh wordcraft-cli convert in.docx out.pdf --strict # wordcraft-cli: strict: 1 character cannot be drawn: U+2D30 (×3) # wordcraft-cli: strict: 1 picture(s) left out: word/media/image2.bin (header2.xml): unsupported format # {"schema":1,"strict":"failed","missing_glyphs":[{"cp":"U+2D30","count":3}],"missing_pictures":[{"part":"word/media/image2.bin","source_part":"word/header2.xml","reason":"unsupported_format"}],"truncated":false,"total_missing_glyphs":1,"total_missing_pictures":1,"glyphs_truncated":false,"pictures_truncated":false} ``` The JSON line (schema 1, also what `file.strictReport` returns) has `schema`, `strict` (`"passed"` or `"failed"`), `missing_glyphs` (entries `{"cp", "count"}`, sorted by code point), `missing_pictures` (entries `{"part", "source_part", "reason"}`: the picture's part or target, the story part it sits in such as `word/header2.xml`, and a reason code; `source_part` is also `background` (the page picture), `body`, `header`, `footer`, `footnote`, `endnote`, `comment` or `text box` where the part name is not known (a document not opened from a DOCX), or a chunk path such as `word/afchunk1.docx > word/header1.xml` for a picture inside an embedded DOCX chunk), `truncated`, the two totals `total_missing_glyphs` and `total_missing_pictures`, and `glyphs_truncated` and `pictures_truncated` for each list. The reason codes are `missing_part`, `external_target`, `link_only`, `undecodable` and `unsupported_format`; the stderr lines use plain words for them. When a list is cut, the stderr line gives the total (`300 characters cannot be drawn (first 256 listed)`). Each list stops at 256 entries separately; `truncated` is true when either was cut, and the totals count every distinct character and picture found, those past the cap included. Only characters the output draws count (not hidden text, or deleted text without `--markup`), and a character a fallback font draws is fine. Text inside a WMF or EMF picture counts too, shaped in the font the picture names with no fallback. A Private Use Area character fails only if no installed font maps it. The result depends on the fonts installed on the host (see #5624 for a fixed font set). An external picture target is never fetched: it is reported, not loaded. Pictures dropped when a DOCX is opened (a missing part, an external target, or a `link only` picture with no embedded copy) are reported for DOCX input only. They have no page, so a PNG of any page is also refused for a missing or external picture anywhere in the document, unused headers included. `render --strict` checks only the page it writes (`--page`; `--scale` doesn't matter), prints nothing on stdout when it refuses, and reports the same way. The engine takes `strict: true` on `file.save`, `file.saveAs`, `file.exportPdf` and `file.exportPng`, and `file.strictReport {markup?, page?}` returns the report without writing. Web: `cd apps/wordcraft-web && trunk serve`, then open . ## For agents: CLI and MCP WordCraft was designed to be driven by people *and* by AI agents. ```sh claude mcp add wordcraft -- wordcraft-cli mcp # headless documents # confine the agent to folders: wordcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root DIR --automation-write-root DIR wordcraft --control 7981 & # or drive the running app… claude mcp add wordcraft-app -- wordcraft-cli mcp --connect 127.0.0.1:7981 ``` Tools include `list_commands`, `execute`, `batch`, `type_text`, `select_text`, `inspect_document`, `render_page`, `save_document`, and, with a running app, `screenshot`, `click` and `key`. Agents can check their work through `inspect_document` without screenshots. See [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) and the [control protocol](docs/control-protocol.md). Macros record any sequence of commands and play it back (`tools.recordMacro`, `tools.macros`). ## Logs The desktop app writes its log records to standard error and to `logs/wordcraft.log` next to its preferences: on Linux `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/wordcraft/logs/` (by default `~/.config/wordcraft/logs/`), on macOS `~/Library/Application Support/WordCraft/logs/`, on Windows `%APPDATA%\WordCraft\logs\`. A start from a desktop menu or the Dock has no terminal, so this file is what to attach to a bug report: unreadable parts of a .docx, pictures or fonts a PDF export had to leave out and panics the command guard recovered from land there. Each launch moves the previous log to `wordcraft.1.log` (and that one to `wordcraft.2.log`), so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start; a log stops growing at 16 MiB. `--version` writes no file, and runs with `WORDCRAFT_NO_PREFS` (agents' test runs) log to standard error only. Document text is never logged; a panic message leaves out the text it quotes. By default WordCraft's own crates log at `info` and everything else at `warn`. `RUST_LOG` replaces that with env_logger-style directives, for example `RUST_LOG=debug`, `RUST_LOG=warn,wordcraft_docx=trace` or `RUST_LOG=info,wgpu_core=warn`; a directive ending in `*` covers every target starting with it (`wordcraft*=debug`). The logger is `apps/wordcraft/src/logging.rs`. ## Architecture | Layer | Crate | Job | |---|---|---| | L0 | `wordcraft-geom` | units and measurements | | L1 | `wordcraft-doc`, `wordcraft-fonts`, `wordcraft-proof` ([`craft-proof`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-libs/tree/main/crates/proof) from craft-libs) | document model and editing; fonts and shaping; spelling, grammar, hyphenation (data: craft-i18n `language-data/`, `CRAFT_I18N_DIR`) | | L2 | `wordcraft-layout`, `wordcraft-docx`, `wordcraft-formats` | line breaking, pagination, tables, notes, hit testing; OOXML; ODT/RTF/HTML/Markdown/TXT | | L3 | `wordcraft-render`, `wordcraft-pdf` | rasteriser (vello_cpu); PDF ([craft-pdf](docs/shared-pdf.md), Krilla) | | L4 | `wordcraft-engine` | session, undo, 422 commands, document feature catalog | | L5 | `wordcraft-mcp` | MCP server | | L6 | `wordcraft-ui-egui` | the word processor front end (swappable) | | apps | `wordcraft`, `wordcraft-cli`, `wordcraft-web` | desktop, command line, browser | `cargo xtask ci` runs formatting, clippy, ~800 tests, the asset-attribution check, the layering check and the wasm build. Contributor and agent instructions: [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). ## Roadmap WordCraft is in **alpha**. It has commands for 97% of the ribbon and menu features in its feature catalog ([`docs/parity-checklist.md`](docs/parity-checklist.md)) today; counting depth, file fidelity, stability and the rest, we estimate it is about 60% ready for real work, about 55% for a typical professional's weekly work and about 63% for everyday essentials. Beta needs testing against real-world .docx files, keeping charts and SmartArt through a round trip, closer pagination fidelity, a stability sweep and native printing. Details and estimates: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) and [where we fall short](docs/gaps.md). ## Downloads **Download WordCraft** from GitHub: the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `wordcraft--windows-x64.msi` | `wordcraft--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `wordcraft--windows-arm64.msi` | `wordcraft--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `wordcraft--windows-x86.msi` | `wordcraft--windows-x86-portable.zip` | The installer is one dual-scope package. By default it installs for your account only, into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ArtCraft\WordCraft`, and needs no administrator rights; choosing "Everyone on this computer" on the first page installs into `C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\WordCraft` (`Program Files (x86)` for the 32-bit build) and asks for an administrator. Install only one copy: a copy for another scope is refused, so uninstall first to change who WordCraft is installed for. Installers and executables are code-signed. **If the app doesn't open on Windows:** the desktop app initializes only DirectX 12 by default. Letting wgpu also create an OpenGL instance can crash some graphics drivers (AMD's `atio6axx.dll`) before the window appears, so the app would flash in Task Manager and quit. `WGPU_BACKEND` overrides the default for troubleshooting (for example `dx12` or `vulkan`). In PowerShell, from the folder containing the executable: ```powershell $env:WGPU_BACKEND = "vulkan" & .\wordcraft.exe Remove-Item Env:WGPU_BACKEND # restore the default for later launches ``` An explicit `gl` override can bring the driver crash back on affected systems. The macOS, Linux and web backend defaults are unchanged. The **32-bit** build uses OpenGL even when a DirectX 12 graphics card is present. On 32-bit Windows, creating a DirectX 12 graphics pipeline fails immediately and the app exits before the window appears. `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan` (or `dx12`) still overrides that. **If the app quits right after its window appears with "Parent device is lost" in the log:** WordCraft compiles DirectX 12 shaders with FXC, the compiler built into Windows, so it needs no `dxcompiler.dll`/`dxil.dll` and ignores any copy another program put on `PATH` (#603). `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER` (`fxc`, `dxc`, `auto`) overrides this; with `dxc`, a matching `dxcompiler.dll` *and* `dxil.dll` must sit next to `wordcraft.exe`. `WGPU_BACKEND = "vulkan"` also avoids DirectX 12 altogether. **If the app is slow on an older Windows PC:** when DirectX 12 finds no graphics card with a driver for it (for example Intel 4th-generation graphics on Windows 11), it only offers the built-in software renderer, which draws every frame on the processor. WordCraft normally uses OpenGL instead, without setting anything. If OpenGL has no usable adapter, it can use DirectX 12's WARP software adapter. The log file records the choice (lines starting with `graphics:`). `WGPU_BACKEND` still overrides it, e.g. `$env:WGPU_BACKEND = "gl"` or `"dx12"`. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `wordcraft--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `wordcraft-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized | ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `wordcraft--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `wordcraft--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Runs anywhere; updates itself with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `wordcraft--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `wordcraft--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed; `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `wordcraft--linux-x86_64.deb` | `wordcraft--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `wordcraft--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `wordcraft--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `wordcraft--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `wordcraft--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `wordcraft--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball cross-compiled for glibc 2.39+ (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 and newer). **Read Aloud** (Review › Read Aloud) speaks through a speech program installed on the system: it tries `espeak-ng`, then `espeak`, and when neither is installed it talks to Speech Dispatcher. The `.rpm` package recommends `espeak-ng`; the `.deb` recommends `espeak-ng` or `speech-dispatcher`, so the package manager installs one of the two by default. With the AppImage or the tarball, install one yourself if neither is there (`sudo apt install espeak-ng`, `sudo dnf install espeak-ng`, `sudo pacman -S espeak-ng`). The Flatpak doesn't speak yet: it has no audio access and doesn't include `espeak-ng`, `espeak` or Speech Dispatcher. **Wayland:** on a Wayland desktop the app runs through XWayland when it is available, because winit (the windowing library) supports dragging files into the window only on X11. To use the native Wayland backend instead (for example for sharper text with fractional scaling, at the cost of file drag-and-drop), choose **File › Options › Advanced › Linux display server › Wayland**; it applies the next time WordCraft starts, and **X11 (XWayland)** or **Automatic** switches back. The `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND` environment variable overrides the setting: `1` for native Wayland, `0` for XWayland: ```sh WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1 wordcraft ``` XWayland needs the X11 libraries, which the packages only recommend and the tarball doesn't install: libX11, libX11-xcb, libXcursor, libXi and libxkbcommon-x11 (on Debian and Ubuntu, `libx11-6`, `libx11-xcb1`, `libxcursor1`, `libxi6` and `libxkbcommon-x11-0`). Without them the app opens on native Wayland, whatever the setting says, and logs which ones are missing. **Arch Linux (AUR).** Community members maintain three AUR packages; the project doesn't publish to the AUR itself. Install one of them: | Package | What it installs | Choose it when | |---|---|---| | [`wordcraft-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/wordcraft-bin) | The release tarball above, prebuilt (x86_64, aarch64) | You want the latest release without compiling (quickest) | | [`wordcraft`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/wordcraft) | The latest release, built from source with `cargo` | You prefer to build releases yourself | | [`wordcraft-git`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/wordcraft-git) | The current `main` branch, built from source | You want unreleased changes and accept an occasional broken build | For example `yay -S wordcraft-bin` or `paru -S wordcraft-bin`. #### Community packages These packages are maintained by community members, not by the WordCraft team. On Gentoo, the [::snakebyte overlay](https://github.com/switch87/snakebyte-overlay) packages the Linux release as `app-office/wordcraft-bin` (prebuilt) and `app-office/wordcraft` (built from source): ```sh eselect repository add snakebyte git https://github.com/switch87/snakebyte-overlay.git emaint sync -r snakebyte echo 'app-office/wordcraft-bin ~amd64' >> /etc/portage/package.accept_keywords/wordcraft emerge --ask app-office/wordcraft-bin ``` ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `wordcraft--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Static site | `wordcraft-web-.zip` | Runs in a modern browser; host it on any static server | ## The Crafting Apps WordCraft is one of the **Crafting Apps**: free, open-source creative tools from the [ArtCraft](https://getartcraft.com/) team, each written from scratch in Rust and each able to stand on its own. | | App | What it's for | Code | Learn more | |:-:|---|---|---|---| | | **PhotoCraft** | Image editing: layers, masks, type and real PSD files | [GitHub](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft) | [Website](https://getartcraft.com/apps/photocraft) | | | **VectorCraft** | Vector illustration | [GitHub](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft) | [Website](https://getartcraft.com/apps/vectorcraft) | | | **FilmCraft** | Video editing, color and sound | [GitHub](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft) | [Website](https://getartcraft.com/apps/filmcraft) | | | **LightCraft** | Photo library and raw development | [GitHub](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft) |
